rows.name: Amazon.com Inc.
rows.statement:
The Committee has reached a BUY recommendation on AMZN with a conviction score of 0.909. The dominant argument, carrying four of five members, is that AWS constitutes a durable franchise of extraordinary earning power — generating approximately 57% of consolidated operating income on 37% annual growth with 39% operating margins — and that its role as the primary infrastructure layer for AI compute represents a secular growth vector not yet fully reflected in current valuations. The most significant dissent came from the value-discipline perspective, which argued that at a $2.81 trillion market cap and 27.66x forward P/E, the stock fails to meet bargain-price criteria and that capital intensity obscures true owner earnings. This dissent did not prevail because the majority concluded that AWS's reinvestment cycle is value-creative rather than value-destructive, with returns on incremental capital substantially exceeding cost of capital. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels.

*Adopted by majority vote of the Furton Research Investment Committee.*

rows.name: Salesforce Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved to assign Salesforce a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.867. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that Salesforce possesses a durable competitive moat — evidenced by eleven consecutive years of CRM market leadership, deeply embedded switching costs across 150,000 enterprise customers, and an increasingly compelling AI monetization trajectory through Agentforce and Data Cloud (AI ARR growing 120% year-over-year to $1.2 billion) — all available at a valuation of approximately 16–18x forward free cash flow that adequately compensates for moderate top-line growth. The most significant dissent, advanced by Mr. Greenblatt, argued that 10% revenue growth at current multiples fails to offer a sufficient margin of safety, with goodwill-laden capital returns obscuring true economics. This objection did not prevail because the majority judged that the combination of expanding margins, substantial free cash flow generation ($15 billion trailing), and the optionality embedded in AI-agent adoption renders the current price a fair-to-attractive entry point rather than a speculative one. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Walt Disney Co.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns DIS a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.84. The dominant argument, endorsed unanimously among the three buying members, holds that Disney possesses a deep, multi-layered competitive moat — spanning theme parks with exceptional pricing power, iconic intellectual property, and an improving streaming economics profile — all available at an attractive valuation of approximately 14.7x forward earnings, meaningfully below broader market multiples. The most significant dissent came from the innovation-oriented perspective, which argued that Disney is not building transformative new platforms and risks structural decline as linear television economics erode. This view did not prevail because the majority concluded that durable franchise value and current price discipline matter more than frontier-market creation potential, and that the valuation already discounts the legacy headwinds without crediting the full earnings power emerging from streaming profitability and segment restructuring. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels, with particular attention to ESPN's direct-to-consumer transition as the key variable warranting ongoing review.

rows.name: Microsoft Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Microsoft Corp. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.75. The dominant argument, advanced by a three-member majority (Aschenbrenner, Wood, Marks), holds that Microsoft's AI monetization trajectory — 43% Azure growth, a $37 billion AI annual run rate expanding at 123% year-over-year, and $678 billion in contracted obligations — represents a discontinuous growth profile that justifies current multiples and renders backward-looking valuation frameworks insufficient. The most significant dissent, articulated by Buffett and Greenblatt, contended that at 27× trailing earnings and 10.6× revenue on a $3.8 trillion market cap, even an extraordinary business offers inadequate margin of safety. This view did not prevail because the majority judged it to be, in Marks's formulation, "first-level thinking dressed in second-level clothing" — anchored to static earnings power rather than the compounding economics of an enterprise AI platform still in early-cycle adoption. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns Alphabet a BUY rating at a score of 0.724. The dominant argument, advanced by Aschenbrenner, Wood, and Marks and carrying the majority, holds that Alphabet's 17x trailing P/E materially undervalues a full-stack AI infrastructure company growing revenue at 24% annually, with Cloud accelerating at 82%, a $514 billion backlog, and proprietary advantages in TPUs, Gemini, and Waymo that position it to capture outsized value as AI revenue scales toward $100 billion. The most significant dissent came from Buffett and Greenblatt, who argued that a 77x EV/FCF multiple, $75 billion in annual capex, and genuine uncertainty around AI disruption to Search economics make owner earnings through 2036 unreliable to underwrite. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the elevated FCF multiple to be a temporary artifact of the capex investment cycle rather than a reflection of structural overvaluation. The Committee recommends initiating a position in GOOGL at current levels.

rows.name: American Express Co.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns American Express a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.65. The dominant argument, advanced by the majority and led by Mr. Buffett and seconded by Mr. Marks, holds that American Express's closed-loop network constitutes a durable structural moat — generating pricing power on both sides of every transaction, sustaining a 36% return on capital, and compounding earnings at a rate that justifies a premium multiple. Mr. Marks further noted that while cycle conditions warrant caution, they do not yet reflect the speculative extremes that would counsel restraint. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Greenblatt, who argued that at approximately 20 times trailing earnings and an EV/EBITDA of 26.47, the current price already reflects the franchise's quality, leaving insufficient margin of safety. This objection did not prevail because the majority concluded that backward-looking valuation comparisons understate the business's forward earnings trajectory. The Committee recommends initiating or maintaining a BUY position at current levels, with valuation monitored on a quarterly basis.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) a final score of **0.577** and recommends a **BUY** position. The dominant argument carrying the majority holds that NVIDIA is not a traditional cyclical hardware company but the central infrastructure node of a generational AI buildout, with data center revenue growing 106% year-over-year, a durable CUDA software moat creating compounding switching costs, and a forward P/E of approximately 18x that inadequately reflects the company's platform-scale growth trajectory — a thesis advanced most forcefully by Ms. Wood and Mr. Aschenbrenner. The most significant dissent, articulated by Messrs. Buffett, Marks, and Greenblatt, argued that at a $5.5 trillion market capitalization, NVIDIA's extraordinary quality is already priced in, with concentrated customer dependency on a handful of hyperscalers introducing material risk of capital expenditure redirection or silicon internalization. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged that the magnitude and durability of the AI infrastructure cycle sufficiently compensate for current valuation levels. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current prices with disciplined sizing reflecting the narrow margin of conviction.

rows.name: Travelers Cos. Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns Travelers a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.375. The dominant argument, advanced by Mr. Buffett and carrying the majority position, held that a business generating a 24.9% core ROE and an 83.6% combined ratio—reflecting genuinely exceptional underwriting discipline—remains attractively valued at 9.58x trailing earnings, representing float produced at negative cost in a manner rarely available at this multiple. The most significant dissent, articulated by Mr. Marks and supported by Mr. Greenblatt, contended that the quality of the franchise is already reflected in the price, noting a 1.97x price-to-book ratio, a four-quarter streak of consensus beats likely pulling optimism forward, and the absence of any special-situation catalyst. This dissent did not prevail because the valuation, while not deeply discounted, remains modest relative to the demonstrated returns on capital, and no evidence was presented that the market has fully capitalized the durability of the underwriting advantage. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position with disciplined sizing consistent with the moderate conviction level.

rows.name: Home Depot Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Home Depot a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.353, reflecting a narrow but affirmative consensus. The dominant argument, advanced principally by Mr. Buffett, held that Home Depot's 51% market share, deeply entrenched Pro contractor relationships, and toll-road economics on the American housing stock constitute a durable franchise whose long-term compounding power justifies acquisition even at current multiples. The most significant dissent, articulated by Mr. Marks and echoed by Mr. Greenblatt, contended that at approximately 23.6x trailing earnings and 27.5x EV/FCF, the market has already priced in the business's quality, leaving insufficient margin of safety amid a frozen housing market and tightening credit conditions. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the franchise's structural advantages and inevitable housing-cycle recovery to outweigh near-term valuation compression risk. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position in HD, with sizing calibrated to reflect the elevated valuation and cyclical uncertainty noted by the minority.

rows.name: Chevron Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Chevron Corporation a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.333, reflecting a narrow and contested majority. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks, held that at an EV/EBITDA of 5.29 and a share price of $201.86, the market has not fully priced the asymmetry between Chevron's demonstrated operational excellence—including $3 billion in structural cost reductions and Hess synergies exceeding targets by 50%—and the potential for cyclical upside, making the risk-reward modestly favorable. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that Chevron's returns on capital remain fundamentally hostage to commodity prices, undermining the durability of the moat and rendering the stock fairly valued rather than compellingly cheap. This dissent did not prevail because Marks's cycle-aware framework demonstrated that current energy-sector valuations offer a margin of safety absent in the broader equity market. The Committee recommends a measured BUY position, sized conservatively to reflect the divided conviction.

rows.name: Nike Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Nike Inc. (NKE) a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.333, reflecting a narrow and qualified majority. The position that carried the committee was advanced by Howard Marks, who argued that Nike's well-documented operational challenges — DTC channel missteps, market-share losses to Hoka and On Running, and China headwinds — are substantially discounted in a stock trading roughly 50% below its highs at 1.27× revenues and 18× trailing earnings, making the risk-reward asymmetry favorable for patient capital. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who contended that a forward P/E of 22.52 still embeds meaningful earnings-recovery expectations that may not materialize given unresolved channel strategy and competitive erosion; their view did not prevail because the committee judged current price dislocation sufficient to compensate for turnaround uncertainty. The Committee recommends a modest initial position with strict downside discipline, to be revisited upon evidence of margin stabilization or further deterioration in competitive standing.

rows.name: Honeywell International Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Honeywell Technologies (HON) a final score of 0.312 and a position of **BUY**. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and carrying the majority, holds that the trailing P/E of 9.39 reflects transitory restructuring distortions rather than fundamental impairment, and that the post-spinoff pure-play automation entity—with segment margins of 19–23%, approximately $4 billion in free cash flow, and a credible organic growth trajectory—offers asymmetric value at current levels within a cycle that has not yet reached speculative excess. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that the wide gap between the trailing and forward P/E (~26.64) implies a substantial earnings recovery already priced in, leaving insufficient margin of safety for a business delivering good-but-not-great returns on capital. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged the restructuring charges to be genuinely non-recurring, making normalized earnings the more appropriate valuation anchor. The Committee recommends initiating a modest position with disciplined sizing reflecting the moderate conviction level.

rows.name: Merck & Co. Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns Merck & Co. a **BUY** rating with a conviction score of **0.312**, reflecting a narrow and qualified majority. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks, held that Keytruda's well-publicized 2028 patent cliff is substantially discounted in the current valuation — a forward P/E of approximately 15x on a dividend-growing franchise with lifecycle management optionalities (subcutaneous reformulation, mRNA combinations) — and that consensus pessimism creates a second-level opportunity for patient capital. The most significant dissent, led by Warren Buffett and supported by Joel Greenblatt and Cathie Wood, centered on the inability to project normalized earnings with confidence given that a single product accounts for roughly half of total revenue, rendering intrinsic value calculations unreliable. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged that the known risk is already embedded in the price, making the risk-reward asymmetry modestly favorable. The Committee recommends a **modest, sized-for-uncertainty position**, with reassessment triggered by material pipeline readouts or further clarity on post-2028 revenue replacement.
